chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'mam ibn al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The artisans/workers, if they stay awake the entire night [working], then their earnings are *suh't* (consumed wealth/unjust gain)."

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Consumed wealth; unjust gain; impermissible earnings

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the earnings of workers who stay up all night working?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the concept of *suh't* (unjust or consumed wealth) to the physical and spiritual neglect inherent in excessive labor. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *mudarrah* (harm) to health as a factor in the validity of earnings, suggesting that while the work itself may be permissible, the resulting depletion of vitality renders the income spiritually deficient or legally suspect due to self-harm.
